```{r functions, include=FALSE}
# All functions used in this deck (the same functions as in the code/ folder),
# defined here so the document knits on its own.

# Rolling CAPM statistics of each fund against the benchmark (monthly returns)
# beta = cov(R_f, R_b) / var(R_b); R2 = cor^2 (share of return variation explained by the market);
# alpha = annualised intercept. Computed from rolling means, so each fund needs Window months of data.
Roll_Beta <- function(Funds, Bench, Window = 36) {

  Funds %>%
    inner_join(Bench %>% select(date, BM = Return), by = "date") %>%
    group_by(Name) %>% arrange(date) %>%
    filter(n() >= Window) %>%
    mutate(mx  = RcppRoll::roll_mean(BM, Window, fill = NA, align = "right"),
           my  = RcppRoll::roll_mean(Return, Window, fill = NA, align = "right"),
           mxy = RcppRoll::roll_mean(BM * Return, Window, fill = NA, align = "right"),
           mxx = RcppRoll::roll_mean(BM^2, Window, fill = NA, align = "right"),
           myy = RcppRoll::roll_mean(Return^2, Window, fill = NA, align = "right")) %>%
    ungroup() %>%
    filter(!is.na(mx)) %>%
    mutate(Beta  = (mxy - mx * my) / (mxx - mx^2),
           R2    = (mxy - mx * my)^2 / ((mxx - mx^2) * (myy - my^2)),
           Alpha = (my - Beta * mx) * 12) %>%
    select(date, Name, Beta, R2, Alpha)

}

# Rolling annualised returns from monthly returns
Roll_Returns_M <- function(df, Months = 12) {

  df %>%
    group_by(Name) %>% arrange(date) %>%
    mutate(RollRet = RcppRoll::roll_prod(1 + Return, n = Months, fill = NA, align = "right")^(12 / Months) - 1) %>%
    ungroup() %>%
    filter(!is.na(RollRet))

}

# Monthly market dispersion: weighted cross-sectional volatility of Capped SWIX constituents,
# using previous month-end weights and monthly (compounded daily) stock returns
Monthly_CSV <- function(Size_Idx, Stock_Rets, Fund = "CappedSWIX") {

  Stock_M <-
    Stock_Rets %>% filter(!is.na(Return)) %>%
    mutate(YM = format(date, "%Y%m")) %>%
    group_by(Tickers, YM) %>%
    summarise(date = max(date), Ret = prod(1 + Return) - 1, .groups = "drop")

  W <-
    Size_Idx %>% filter(Fund == !!Fund) %>%
    mutate(YM = format(date %m+% months(1), "%Y%m")) %>%      # weights at end of t-1 apply in month t
    select(YM, Tickers, Weight)

  Stock_M %>%
    inner_join(W, by = c("YM", "Tickers")) %>%
    group_by(YM) %>%
    mutate(w = Weight / sum(Weight)) %>%
    summarise(date = max(date), CSV = sqrt(sum(w * (Ret - sum(w * Ret))^2)), .groups = "drop")

}
```

```{r data_prep, include=FALSE}
Active_Manager_Peers <- read_rds("data/Active_Managers.rds") %>% rename(Return = Returns)
ABC_Fund <- read_rds("data/ABC_Fund.rds") %>% rename(Return = Returns)
Idx_Daily <- read_rds("data/Index_Returns_Daily.rds")
Size_Idx <- read_rds("data/Monthly_Index_Constituents.rds")
Stock_Rets <- read_rds("data/Stock_Returns_Daily.rds") %>%
  select(date, Tickers, Return = Returns) %>%
  mutate(Return = ifelse(abs(Return) > 0.5, NA, Return))

# Benchmark: daily Capped SWIX compounded to calendar month-ends
Bench_M <- Idx_Daily %>% filter(Tickers == "J433") %>%
  mutate(YM = format(date, "%Y%m")) %>%
  group_by(YM) %>% summarise(Return = prod(1 + Returns) - 1, .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(date = ceiling_date(ymd(paste0(YM, "01")), "month") - days(1)) %>% select(date, Return)

Funds <- bind_rows(Active_Manager_Peers, ABC_Fund) %>%
  mutate(Type = ifelse(Name == "ABC_Fund", "ABC Fund", "Peers"))
Peer_Med <- Active_Manager_Peers %>% group_by(date) %>% summarise(PeerMed = median(Return))

# Rolling beta
RB <- Roll_Beta(Funds %>% select(date, Name, Return), Bench_M, Window = 36) %>%
  mutate(Type = ifelse(Name == "ABC_Fund", "ABC Fund", "Peers"))
RB_Sum <- RB %>% group_by(Type) %>% summarise(Beta = median(Beta), R2 = median(R2), Alpha = median(Alpha))
ABC_Beta_Now <- RB %>% filter(date == max(date)) %>% mutate(Pct = percent_rank(Beta)) %>% filter(Type == "ABC Fund")

# Drivers: PCA on peers with full history since 2015
PCA_Panel <- Active_Manager_Peers %>% filter(date >= ymd(20150131)) %>%
  group_by(Name) %>% filter(n() == 130) %>% ungroup() %>% spread(Name, Return)
pca <- prcomp(PCA_Panel %>% select(-date), scale. = TRUE)
PC1_Share <- summary(pca)$importance[2, 1]
PC <- tibble(date = PCA_Panel$date, PC1 = pca$x[, 1])
Funds_PC <- Funds %>% inner_join(PC, by = "date") %>% group_by(Name, Type) %>% filter(n() >= 60) %>%
  summarise(R2_PC1 = cor(Return, PC1)^2, .groups = "drop")
Cor_Peer <- Funds %>% filter(date >= ymd(20150131)) %>%
  inner_join(Peer_Med, by = "date") %>% inner_join(Bench_M %>% rename(BM = Return), by = "date") %>%
  group_by(Name, Type) %>% filter(n() >= 60) %>%
  summarise(Cor_Peer = cor(Return, PeerMed), TE = sd(Return - BM) * sqrt(12), .groups = "drop") %>%
  left_join(Funds_PC %>% select(Name, R2_PC1), by = "Name")

# Relative performance
RR <- Roll_Returns_M(Funds %>% select(date, Name, Return), 12)
Bands <- RR %>% filter(Name != "ABC_Fund") %>% group_by(date) %>%
  summarise(q05 = quantile(RollRet, .05), q25 = quantile(RollRet, .25), q50 = median(RollRet),
            q75 = quantile(RollRet, .75), q95 = quantile(RollRet, .95), .groups = "drop") %>%
  inner_join(RR %>% filter(Name == "ABC_Fund") %>% select(date, ABC = RollRet), by = "date")
Rank <- RR %>% group_by(date) %>% filter(any(Name == "ABC_Fund")) %>%
  mutate(Pct = percent_rank(RollRet)) %>% filter(Name == "ABC_Fund") %>% ungroup()
Track <- Funds %>% filter(Name == "ABC_Fund", date >= ymd(20150131)) %>% select(date, ABC = Return) %>%
  inner_join(Peer_Med, by = "date") %>% inner_join(Bench_M %>% rename(BM = Return), by = "date")

# Dispersion
CSV_M <- Monthly_CSV(Size_Idx, Stock_Rets)
D <- Track %>% mutate(YM = format(date, "%Y%m")) %>% inner_join(CSV_M %>% select(YM, CSV), by = "YM") %>%
  mutate(Regime = case_when(CSV >= quantile(CSV, 0.8) ~ "High dispersion",
                            CSV <= quantile(CSV, 0.2) ~ "Low dispersion", TRUE ~ "Normal"))
R12 <- D %>% arrange(date) %>%
  mutate(Rel12 = RcppRoll::roll_sum(ABC - PeerMed, 12, fill = NA, align = "right"),
         CSV12 = RcppRoll::roll_mean(CSV, 12, fill = NA, align = "right")) %>%
  filter(!is.na(Rel12)) %>%
  mutate(Reg = case_when(CSV12 >= quantile(CSV12, 0.8) ~ "High", CSV12 <= quantile(CSV12, 0.2) ~ "Low", TRUE ~ "Normal"))
```

## The case for ABC Fund in three points

- **Most active managers mostly deliver market beta.** The typical peer has a beta of `r round(RB_Sum$Beta[RB_Sum$Type == "Peers"], 2)`, and the market explains `r round(RB_Sum$R2[RB_Sum$Type == "Peers"] * 100)`% of its returns.
- **ABC Fund is genuinely different.** Its beta is now `r round(ABC_Beta_Now$Beta, 2)`, lower than `r round(ABC_Beta_Now$Pct * 100)`% of peers, and its returns follow its own decisions rather than the industry consensus.
- **The difference has paid off.** Since 2015 ABC has beaten both the typical peer and the benchmark, with less volatility, and it protects capital best when markets fall.

## The industry is mostly market beta

```{r beta_plot}
RB %>% filter(month(date) == 12 | date == max(date)) %>% mutate(Year = factor(year(date))) %>%
  ggplot(aes(Year, Beta)) +
  geom_jitter(data = . %>% filter(Type == "Peers"), color = "grey60", alpha = 0.5, width = 0.2, size = 1.2) +
  geom_boxplot(data = . %>% filter(Type == "Peers"), fill = NA, outlier.shape = NA, color = "steelblue", linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_point(data = . %>% filter(Type == "ABC Fund"), color = "red", size = 5, shape = 18) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 1, linetype = 2, color = "grey40") +
  labs(title = "Rolling 3-year beta to the Capped SWIX (each December)",
       subtitle = "Grey: active peers. Red: ABC Fund. Dashed: the market (beta = 1)",
       x = "", y = "Beta") +
  Slide_Theme
```

## Track record since 2015

```{r track_table}
tibble(
  Measure = c("Annualised return", "Annualised volatility", "Return per unit of risk",
              "Rolling 3-year beta (median)", "Alpha (annualised, median)"),
  `ABC Fund` = c(prod(1 + Track$ABC)^(12 / nrow(Track)) - 1, sd(Track$ABC) * sqrt(12),
                 (prod(1 + Track$ABC)^(12 / nrow(Track)) - 1) / (sd(Track$ABC) * sqrt(12)),
                 RB_Sum$Beta[RB_Sum$Type == "ABC Fund"], RB_Sum$Alpha[RB_Sum$Type == "ABC Fund"]),
  `Typical peer` = c(prod(1 + Track$PeerMed)^(12 / nrow(Track)) - 1, sd(Track$PeerMed) * sqrt(12),
                     (prod(1 + Track$PeerMed)^(12 / nrow(Track)) - 1) / (sd(Track$PeerMed) * sqrt(12)),
                     RB_Sum$Beta[RB_Sum$Type == "Peers"], RB_Sum$Alpha[RB_Sum$Type == "Peers"]),
  `Capped SWIX` = c(prod(1 + Track$BM)^(12 / nrow(Track)) - 1, sd(Track$BM) * sqrt(12),
                    (prod(1 + Track$BM)^(12 / nrow(Track)) - 1) / (sd(Track$BM) * sqrt(12)), 1, 0)) %>%
  mutate(across(-Measure, ~ ifelse(Measure %in% c("Return per unit of risk", "Rolling 3-year beta (median)"),
                                   sprintf("%.2f", .), sprintf("%.1f%%", . * 100)))) %>%
  flextable() %>% fontsize(size = 16, part = "all") %>% bold(part = "header") %>%
  bg(j = "ABC Fund", bg = "#FDE2E2", part = "body") %>%
  add_footer_lines("January 2015 to October 2025, monthly returns. Typical peer = median active manager each month.") %>%
  fontsize(size = 12, part = "footer") %>% autofit()
```

## Where the edge comes from: falling markets

```{r updown_plot}
D %>% mutate(Market = ifelse(BM < 0, "Months the market fell", "Months the market rose")) %>%
  group_by(Market) %>%
  summarise(`ABC Fund` = mean(ABC) * 12, `Typical peer` = mean(PeerMed) * 12, `Capped SWIX` = mean(BM) * 12,
            Hit = mean(ABC > PeerMed), .groups = "drop") %>%
  gather(Fund, Ret, `ABC Fund`, `Typical peer`, `Capped SWIX`) %>%
  mutate(Fund = factor(Fund, levels = c("ABC Fund", "Typical peer", "Capped SWIX"),
                       labels = c("ABC\nFund", "Typical\npeer", "Capped\nSWIX"))) %>%
  ggplot(aes(Fund, Ret, fill = Fund)) + geom_col(width = 0.6) +
  geom_text(aes(label = scales::percent(Ret, accuracy = 1), vjust = ifelse(Ret < 0, 1.4, -0.5)), size = 5) +
  facet_wrap(~Market, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("red", "grey55", "steelblue")) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent, expand = expansion(mult = 0.18)) +
  labs(title = "Average return in falling and rising months (annualised)",
       subtitle = paste0("ABC beat the typical peer in ",
                         round(mean(D$ABC[D$BM < 0] > D$PeerMed[D$BM < 0]) * 100), "% of the months the market fell"),
       x = "", y = "") +
  Slide_Theme + theme(legend.position = "none")
```

## Does high market dispersion reward ABC?

```{r disp_plot}
R12 %>% ggplot(aes(CSV12, Rel12)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, color = "grey40") +
  geom_point(aes(color = Reg), size = 3, alpha = 0.8) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE, color = "black", linewidth = 0.8) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c(High = "red", Low = "steelblue", Normal = "grey60"), name = "Dispersion") +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent) + scale_x_continuous(labels = scales::percent) +
  labs(title = "Over 12 months, yes: ABC's edge grows when stocks diverge",
       subtitle = paste0("Each dot is a 12-month window. ABC beat the typical peer in ",
                         round(mean(R12$Rel12[R12$Reg == "High"] > 0) * 100), "% of high-dispersion windows"),
       x = "Average market dispersion over 12 months", y = "ABC return minus typical peer") +
  Slide_Theme
```

## Dispersion: what we can and cannot say

- **Over a year or more, the claim holds.** In the most dispersed 12-month periods ABC beat the typical peer by `r round(mean(R12$Rel12[R12$Reg == "High"]) * 100, 1)`%, against `r round(mean(R12$Rel12[R12$Reg != "High"]) * 100, 1)`% in other periods.
- **Month to month, it does not.** In the single most dispersed months ABC actually lagged its peers (it beat them in only `r round(mean(D$ABC[D$Regime == "High dispersion"] > D$PeerMed[D$Regime == "High dispersion"]) * 100)`% of those months).
- **Most of the evidence comes from one period (2020-2022).** We suggest presenting dispersion as supporting colour, and leading with ABC's low beta and downside protection.

## Why ABC belongs in client portfolios

- **Something other than market beta:** clients can buy beta cheaply in an index fund; ABC offers a different return stream.
- **A better ride:** higher returns than the typical peer and the benchmark since 2015, with less volatility.
- **Protection when it matters:** ABC has done best when markets fall, which is when clients need it most.
- **Caveats:** past performance does not guarantee future returns; the analysis uses returns only and covers 2015-2025, and ABC tends to lag in strong rising markets.
